note: Human review of the derived ligament attachments, applied by src/scripts/generateLigamentSeed.ts. Derivation measures which bones a ligament mesh TOUCHES; this file records where touching is not attaching, and where a human has confirmed that it is. An entry with `confirmed: true` and no `attachmentStructureIds` keeps the derived set and only clears needsReview. Regenerating the seed re-applies this file, so a correction is never lost to a re-run. Entries sourced to the review page are the user's own ticks, read back from the artifact database.

deep-transverse-metatarsal-ligament.description: A series of short transverse bands joining the plantar plates of adjacent metatarsophalangeal joints, binding the heads of the metatarsals together and holding the forefoot as a unit.
deep-transverse-metatarsal-ligament.source: Labelled dorsal foot diagram and Netter plantar/lateral foot plate, supplied 13 Sept 2026
deep-transverse-metatarsal-ligament.why: It runs head to head between the plantar plates and never reaches a phalanx. The derived contact with the proximal phalanges is the mesh lying against their bases — the clearest case in the tranche of touching not being attaching.

deep-transverse-metacarpal-ligament.description: Short transverse bands joining the palmar plates of the second to fifth metacarpophalangeal joints, binding the metacarpal heads together. The thumb is free of it, which is part of why it opposes.
deep-transverse-metacarpal-ligament.source: By the same anatomy as the foot band above, which the supplied plates settle; standard teaching for the hand
deep-transverse-metacarpal-ligament.why: The hand's band is the metatarsal band's counterpart and attaches the same way — plate to plate across the metacarpal heads, not to the phalanges. Derivation put the metacarpals top anyway (3rd 22%, 2nd 17%, 4th 17%).

ulnolunate-ligament.description: A palmar ulnocarpal ligament running from the ulna, by way of the palmar radioulnar ligament and the triangular fibrocartilage, to the lunate.
ulnolunate-ligament.source: Labelled palmar wrist plate supplied 13 Sept 2026 (ulnolunate drawn from the ulnar head region to the lunate)
ulnolunate-ligament.why: It arises with the palmar radioulnar ligament and inserts on the lunate. The derived scaphoid and capitate contact is the strap lying against the carpus on its way; only the lunate is an attachment.

popliteofibular-ligament.description: A deep posterolateral band running from the popliteus tendon to the styloid process of the fibular head, resisting external rotation of the tibia.
popliteofibular-ligament.why: Only the fibula is a bony attachment. The other end is the popliteus tendon, which the app does not model as a structure, so one bone is the complete bony answer rather than a missing second one.

posterior-meniscotibial-ligament-medial-.description: The posterior part of the coronary ligament of the medial meniscus, anchoring the meniscal rim to the margin of the tibial plateau.
posterior-meniscotibial-ligament-medial-.why: Tibia is the only bony end; the other attaches to the medial meniscus, which is not a bone. The derivation reporting one bone is correct, not incomplete.

external-intercostal-membrane.description: The aponeurotic sheet continuing the external intercostal muscle forwards between the costal cartilages.
external-intercostal-membrane.why: It spans costal cartilage, not bone, and the app models no cartilage structures — so an empty bony attachment list is the honest answer. It carries no attachment question, only locate and identify.

posterior-meniscotibial-ligament-lateral.description: The posterior part of the coronary ligament of the lateral meniscus, anchoring the meniscal rim to the margin of the tibial plateau.
posterior-meniscotibial-ligament-lateral.source: Review page, marked corrected with no attachment change, 13 Sept 2026
posterior-meniscotibial-ligament-lateral.why: The reviewer marked this corrected but left the attachment field blank, which the page defines as "the attachments are right but something else is wrong". Tibia is right — the other end is the meniscus. What is wrong is that it can barely be seen: even with the meniscus ghosted it traces at 0.06% of frame at a single angle, the smallest target in the tranche. Flagged for a keep-or-drop decision; the attachment itself is settled.

tibionavicular-ligament.description: The most anterior band of the superficial deltoid ligament. It runs from the anterior colliculus of the medial malleolus to the dorsomedial tuberosity of the navicular, crossing the ankle and talonavicular joints on its way — which is why the mesh touches the talus without attaching to it.

costoclavicular-ligament.description: A short, strong band binding the underside of the medial clavicle, at the rhomboid fossa, to the first costal cartilage and the adjacent end of the first rib. It is the main restraint on elevation of the medial clavicle.

long-plantar-ligament.description: The longest ligament of the foot. It runs from the plantar calcaneus in front of the tuberosity to the ridge of the cuboid, where its deep fibres insert; the superficial fibres carry on to the bases of the second to fourth metatarsals, variably the fifth. It roofs the cuboid groove, turning it into the canal for peroneus longus.

acetabular-labrum.description: A fibrocartilaginous ring attached to the bony rim of the acetabulum and, across the acetabular notch, to the transverse acetabular ligament. It deepens the socket and seals it; the femoral head sits within it but the labrum does not attach to the femur.

glenoid-labrum.description: A fibrocartilaginous rim attached around the circumference of the glenoid cavity of the scapula, deepening the socket and anchoring the long head of biceps at its superior pole. The humeral head articulates against it.

annular-ligament-of-radius.description: A ring attached by both of its ends to the anterior and posterior margins of the radial notch of the ulna, forming about four-fifths of an osseofibrous collar that encircles the head of the radius and holds it against the ulna while it spins.

meniscopatellar-ligament.description: The medial patellomeniscal ligament: it runs from the medial meniscus to the distal pole of the patella, a few millimetres above its lower border. Only one end of it is bone.

intersesamoid-ligament.description: A short fibrous band joining the two sesamoid bones under the head of the first metatarsal, the medial (tibial) to the lateral (fibular). Its upper surface is grooved, and the tendon of flexor hallucis longus runs in that groove.

interspinous-ligaments.description: Thin sheets filling the gap between adjacent spinous processes, running from the root of one to its apex, a single segment at a time, from the neck to the sacrum. They blend with the ligamentum flavum in front and the supraspinous ligament behind. They are best developed at the thoracolumbar junction and in the lumbar spine, slight in the neck and thin or effectively absent in the upper thoracic spine.

costotransverse-ligament.description: Runs from the back of the neck of a rib to the front of the transverse process of its own thoracic vertebra, binding the two together. It is diminished or absent at the eleventh and twelfth ribs, which have no costotransverse joint.

supraspinous-ligament.description: A cord-like band joining the tips of the spinous processes, continuous above with the nuchal ligament. Classically described as running from C7 to the sacrum (TA98), though in practice it is well developed only to the upper lumbar spine: it most often ends at L4, occasionally L3, reaches L5 in about one person in twenty, and is almost always absent at L5/S1.

ligamenta-flava.description: Short, elastic sheets joining the laminae of adjacent vertebral arches from C2 down to the sacrum, each running from the front of the lamina above to the back of the lamina below. Their elastin puts the spine under gentle tension and helps it straighten after bending.

anterior-longitudinal-ligament.description: A broad band running the whole length of the front of the vertebral column, from the anterior tubercle of the atlas and the base of the skull to the sacrum. It is attached to the front of every vertebral body and lies against the discs between them, and it is the main check on extension.

posterior-longitudinal-ligament.description: Runs the length of the back of the vertebral bodies, inside the vertebral canal, from the body of the axis to the sacrum, continuous above with the tectorial membrane. Its fibres blend with each annulus and the neighbouring endplates, and it is narrow behind the mid-body, which is why discs herniate posterolaterally.

dorsal-radiocarpal-ligament.description: A broad oblique band on the back of the wrist running from the dorsal rim of the distal radius, across the lunate, to the dorsal tubercle of the triquetrum. It reinforces the dorsal capsule of the radiocarpal joint and limits full wrist flexion.

dorsal-radiocarpal-ligament.quote: The dorsal radiocarpal ligament forms a part of the dorsal radiocarpal joint capsule and connects the dorsal radial rim with the lunate and triquetral bone.
dorsal-radiocarpal-ligament.why: The seed included the scaphoid; the ligament is the radiolunotriquetral band and no retrieved source gives it a scaphoid attachment.

dorsal-ulnocarpal-ligament.description: A capsular band on the ulnar side of the back of the wrist running from the styloid process of the ulna down to the triquetrum. It reinforces the dorsal capsule of the radiocarpal joint and helps steady the carpus on the ulna during forearm rotation.
dorsal-ulnocarpal-ligament.source: Source check, 22 Sep 2026: each row fetched and quoted from the work cited
dorsal-ulnocarpal-ligament.quote: It attaches proximally to the styloid process of the distal ulna and extends distally to the triquetrum
dorsal-ulnocarpal-ligament.why: The seed added the lunate and scaphoid, which belong to the palmar ulnocarpal complex rather than the dorsal band. Disputed: IMAIOS treats it as part of a wider ulnocarpal complex with ulnocapitate, ulnolunate and ulnotriquetral components; the classic dorsal band itself is described as ulna to triquetrum only.

interosseous-metacarpal-ligaments.description: Short deep bands set between the touching side surfaces of the bases of the second to fifth metacarpals, just beyond their small articular facets. They are the strongest of the intermetacarpal ligaments and lock the metacarpal bases into a stable arch.
interosseous-metacarpal-ligaments.source: Source check, 22 Sep 2026: each row fetched and quoted from the work cited
interosseous-metacarpal-ligaments.quote: The bases of the second, third, fourth and fifth metacarpal bones articulate with one another by small surfaces covered with cartilage, and are connected together by dorsal, volar, and interosseous ligaments
interosseous-metacarpal-ligaments.why: The seed added the trapezium, which no source gives; the trapezium contact is the ligament group lying against it at the thumb base. Disputed: The older Gray's usage applies the same name to the deep bands joining the capitate and hamate to the third and fourth metacarpal bases; Terminologia Anatomica places ligamenta metacarpea interossea with the intermetacarpal joints, between the metacarpal bases, which is the reading used here.

palmar-capitohamate-ligament.description: A short thick band on the palmar side of the wrist joining the capitate to the hamate. It is one of the interosseous ligaments that lock the distal carpal row into a rigid unit.
palmar-capitohamate-ligament.source: Source check, 22 Sep 2026: each row fetched and quoted from the work cited

palmar-capitohamate-ligament.why: The seed's capitate and hamate pair matches the source; the deep part is described as extending towards the third and fourth metacarpal bases but the palmar band itself stays within the capitohamate joint.

palmar-carpometacarpal-ligaments.description: A set of short oblique bands on the palm of the hand running from the distal row of carpal bones, the trapezium, trapezoid, capitate and hamate, onto the bases of the metacarpals. They tie the metacarpals to the carpus and keep the carpometacarpal joints of the fingers almost rigid.
palmar-carpometacarpal-ligaments.source: Source check, 22 Sep 2026: each row fetched and quoted from the work cited
palmar-carpometacarpal-ligaments.quote: The palmar carpometacarpal ligaments (volar ligaments) have a somewhat similar arrangement, with the exception of those of the third metacarpal, which are three in number: a lateral one from the greater multangular, situated superficial to the sheath of the tendon of the Flexor carpi radialis; and intermediate one from the capitate; and a medial one from the hamate.
palmar-carpometacarpal-ligaments.why: The seed named only the trapezium and hamate; the capitate is named explicitly in the source and the trapezoid follows from Kenhub's description of bands from the whole distal carpal row.

palmar-lunotriquetral-ligament.description: The palmar band of the lunotriquetral ligament, joining the lunate to the triquetrum on the front of the wrist. It is the strongest part of that ligament and is a major restraint holding the proximal carpal row together.
palmar-lunotriquetral-ligament.source: Source check, 22 Sep 2026: each row fetched and quoted from the work cited

palmar-lunotriquetral-ligament.why: The seed's lunate and triquetrum pair matches the source exactly.

palmar-metacarpal-ligaments.description: Short transverse bands running across the palmar surfaces of the bases of the second to fifth metacarpals, joining each one to its neighbour. They hold the metacarpal bases together and support the transverse arch of the palm.
palmar-metacarpal-ligaments.source: Source check, 22 Sep 2026: each row fetched and quoted from the work cited
palmar-metacarpal-ligaments.quote: The dorsal and palmar metacarpal ligaments pass transversely from one bone to another on the dorsal and volar surfaces of the bases of the second, third, fourth and fifth metacarpal bones.
palmar-metacarpal-ligaments.why: The seed's grouped metacarpals id is right; the first metacarpal contact is incidental as these bands span the second to fifth bases.

pisohamate-ligament.description: A short band running from the pisiform to the hook of the hamate, effectively a continuation of the flexor carpi ulnaris tendon. It anchors the pisiform and forms the roof of Guyon's canal, through which the ulnar nerve and artery pass.

pisohamate-ligament.quote: The pisiform bone is also connected to the hook of hamate bone and fifth metacarpal bones via pisohamate and pisometacarpal ligaments, respectively.
pisohamate-ligament.why: The seed's pisiform and hamate pair matches the source; the distal attachment is specifically the hook of the hamate, for which the app also has a hook-of-hamate id if a finer target is wanted.

pisometacarpal-ligament.description: Runs from the palmar surface of the pisiform to the base of the fifth metacarpal, as a distal prolongation of the flexor carpi ulnaris tendon. It anchors the pisiform and stabilises the pisotriquetral joint as the wrist is flexed.

pisometacarpal-ligament.why: Seed is right; the grouped metacarpals id covers the fifth (and, per Radsource, sometimes fourth) metacarpal base.

pisotriquetral-ligament.description: A capsular thickening running from the dorsal aspect of the pisiform to the triquetrum, with radial and ulnar components. It is the main stabiliser of the pisotriquetral joint, resisting sideways translation of the pisiform.
pisotriquetral-ligament.source: Source check, 22 Sep 2026: each row fetched and quoted from the work cited
pisotriquetral-ligament.quote: Joins the dorsal aspect of the pisiform to the triquetrum
pisotriquetral-ligament.why: Seed is right; the ligament is confined to the pisiform-triquetrum pair and the mesh contacts match.

radial-collateral-ligament-of-wrist-join.description: Runs from the tip of the radial styloid process to the radial side of the scaphoid, with some fibres carrying on to the trapezium. It limits ulnar deviation of the wrist.
radial-collateral-ligament-of-wrist-join.source: Source check, 22 Sep 2026: each row fetched and quoted from the work cited
sources: Radial collateral ligament of wrist joint - Wikipedia (text from Gray's Anatomy, 20th ed.). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radial_collateral_ligament_of_wrist_joint
radial-collateral-ligament-of-wrist-join.quote: The radial collateral ligament (external lateral ligament, radial carpal collateral ligament) extends from the tip of the styloid process of the radius and attaches to the radial side of the scaphoid (formerly navicular bone of the hand), immediately adjacent to its proximal articular surface and some fibres extend to the lateral side of the trapezium (greater multangular bone).
radial-collateral-ligament-of-wrist-join.why: Seed is right; the radial attachment is specifically the radial styloid process, which the app models only as part of the radius here.

radiocapitate-ligament.description: A palmar wrist ligament running from the radial styloid process obliquely across the wrist to the palmar surface of the capitate. It helps hold the carpus against the radius and resists ulnar translation of the carpal bones.
radiocapitate-ligament.source: Source check, 22 Sep 2026: each row fetched and quoted from the work cited
radiocapitate-ligament.quote: a palmar (volar) extrinsic radiocarpal ligament that originates from the radial styloid process and courses distally and ulnarly to insert onto the palmar aspect of the capitate
radiocapitate-ligament.why: Seed is right on attachments; the only question in the literature is whether this is a distinct ligament rather than part of the radioscaphocapitate. Disputed: Whether the radiocapitate ligament is a separate ligament at all: Terminologia Anatomica 2 lists it as an inconstant term, and several authors treat it as a portion or variant of the radioscaphocapitate ligament. Its radius-to-capitate course is not in doubt.

radioscaphocapitate-ligament.description: Runs from the radial styloid process across the waist of the scaphoid to the palmar surface of the capitate. It is one of the strongest palmar wrist ligaments, acting as a sling that supports the scaphoid and stops the carpus sliding ulnarwards.
radioscaphocapitate-ligament.source: Source check, 22 Sep 2026: each row fetched and quoted from the work cited
radioscaphocapitate-ligament.quote: Inserts on distal aspect of scaphoid, proximal capitate
radioscaphocapitate-ligament.why: Seed is right: all three bones carry fibres, even though the scaphoid share is partly a wrap rather than a firm insertion. Disputed: How much of the ligament truly inserts into the scaphoid is debated; some authors describe the scaphoid contact as mainly a sling over the waist with only a minor bony insertion into the capitate body.

scaphocapitate-ligament.description: A short palmar ligament running from the distal pole of the scaphoid to the palmar surface of the capitate. It is one of the palmar midcarpal ligaments and keeps the scaphoid from collapsing into flexion.
scaphocapitate-ligament.source: Source check, 22 Sep 2026: each row fetched and quoted from the work cited
scaphocapitate-ligament.quote: The scaphocapitate ligament is attached proximally on the distal pole of the scaphoid and distally on the palmar cortex of the capitate.
scaphocapitate-ligament.why: Seed is right; a clean two-bone ligament matching the mesh contacts.

scaphotrapeziotrapezoidal-ligament.description: A complex of short palmar and dorsal bands running from the distal pole of the scaphoid to the trapezium and trapezoid. It stabilises the scaphotrapeziotrapezoid joint and resists flexion of the scaphoid.
scaphotrapeziotrapezoidal-ligament.source: Source check, 22 Sep 2026: each row fetched and quoted from the work cited
scaphotrapeziotrapezoidal-ligament.quote: Originates at the radial/ulnar surfaces of the distal pole of the scaphoid … Inserts distally at the volar/radial surfaces off the trapezium, volar surface of the trapezoid
scaphotrapeziotrapezoidal-ligament.why: Seed wrongly listed the capitate, which the mesh only passes close to; the ligament is named for and attaches to the scaphoid, trapezium and trapezoid. Disputed: Some authors fold the palmar scaphocapitate ligament into the wider STT ligament complex, which is where a capitate attachment would come from; the STT ligament itself spans only scaphoid, trapezium and trapezoid.

triquetrocapitate-ligament.description: Runs from the distal radial corner of the triquetrum to the ulnar side of the capitate. It is one of the palmar midcarpal ligaments and forms the ulnar limb of the arcuate ligament that stabilises the midcarpal joint.
triquetrocapitate-ligament.source: Source check, 22 Sep 2026: each row fetched and quoted from the work cited
triquetrocapitate-ligament.quote: The triquetrocapitate ligament attaches proximally to the triquetrum at its distal and radial corner, and distally at the ulnar side of the capitate, running radially to the triquetrohamate ligament.
triquetrocapitate-ligament.why: Seed wrongly included the hamate; the ligament only runs ulnar to the neighbouring triquetrohamate ligament and the mesh merely brushes the hamate.

triquetrohamate-ligament.description: Runs from the distal palmar margin of the triquetrum to the palmar surface of the hamate, just ulnar to the triquetrocapitate ligament. It steadies the ulnar side of the midcarpal joint.
triquetrohamate-ligament.source: Source check, 22 Sep 2026: each row fetched and quoted from the work cited
triquetrohamate-ligament.quote: The triquetrohamate ligament attaches proximally at the distal margin of the palmar cortex of the triquetrum and distally at the palmar cortex of the hamate, running ulnar to the triquetrocapitate ligament.
triquetrohamate-ligament.why: Seed is right; a clean two-bone ligament matching the mesh contacts.

ulnar-collateral-ligament-of-wrist-joint.description: A cord running from the tip of the ulnar styloid process and splitting into two bands, one to the medial side of the triquetrum and one to the pisiform and flexor retinaculum. It limits radial deviation of the wrist.

ulnar-collateral-ligament-of-wrist-joint.quote: The ulnar collateral ligament is a rounded cord, attached above to the end of the styloid process of the ulna, and dividing below into two fasciculi, one of which is attached to the medial side of the triquetral bone, the other to the pisiform and flexor retinaculum.
ulnar-collateral-ligament-of-wrist-joint.why: Seed wrongly included the lunate, which the mesh only grazes at 8 per cent; the classical description lists only the ulnar styloid, triquetrum and pisiform (plus the flexor retinaculum, which the app does not model). Disputed: Nomenclature only: Kenhub and some modern texts treat this ligament as the ulnotriquetral division of the palmar ulnocarpal ligament rather than a true collateral ligament. No source gives it a lunate attachment.
